title: Earpiece
brief: Invent one new widget that goes beyond everything in the catalog. One remarkable idea, or none.

stamps.reason: An automatic aside-widget question in the calibration/proof/critic family, and it pays a cache-read of the whole context on every editing turn for a self-report nobody can check.
stamps.subject: Fine print

stamps.reason: The same widget as Loupe from the same order, widened with a port lookup that does not belong on the card.
stamps.subject: Lens

stamps.reason: The answered half of owed-widget and parking-widget: a log read once a month that nobody would mention to a colleague.
stamps.subject: Decisions

stamps.reason: Keeping deleted drafts on screen costs more in privacy than a novelty line gives, and the rescue of a wiped draft is too rare to carry a card.
stamps.subject: Unsent

stamps.reason: A word-list match over the stream that stream-widget and marquee-widget already tap, noisy on ordinary uses of 'actually' and empty where thinking is not shown.
stamps.subject: Double take

stamps.reason: Dropping a prompt on a capitals-and-punctuation guess makes every false hold cost the person a send, which is out of proportion to a joke told once.
stamps.subject: Count to ten

stamps.reason: Not chosen: a real new input (the mouse selection) but fullscreen only, its answer is a git grep guess at a definition, and it only looks things up where Earpiece changes how the work goes.
stamps.subject: Loupe

stamps.reason: Not chosen: useful, but it is a fixed pattern list over tool.call edits, the shape footprint, proof and todos already have, with false alarms on 'as any' and 'noqa'; it does not go beyond the catalog as the order asks.
stamps.subject: Corners

stamps.reason: Earpiece is the only idea that does something no widget and no part of the catalog can: read inside a running subagent and correct it without stopping the turn, at no token cost, on calls that all exist.
Every call exists in the types file, all main states are drawn and fit at 20 columns, the second command is justified and the spec is within size; 15 notes for the machinist in spec-notes.md.

A4 and A6 cannot be tested as written: in claude plugin test (2.1.289) a plugin's $.session.append always rejects with 'HooksError: no implementation for session.append' before any hook runs, so no test hook, ground() answer, other plugin or engine.create stand-in can record the append, answer it with a uuid or answer { deny } (a test hook that answers the event without next is skipped; session.send, agent.list and session.messages stand in fine). Tests can only prove the reject-then-send path; rewrite A4/A6 and the Acceptance preamble so the successful append and its { deny } branch are proven by the Live run, or name another seam. register.tsx, types and widget.json are built to the spec and validate; tests/widget.test.tsx is still the scaffold stub.

The build's send-back is answered: A4, A6 and the Acceptance preamble now prove the reject-then-send path under test and leave the uuid append to the Live run, with no contradiction, no new call and the spec at 120 lines and 15 acceptance lines; 17 notes for the machinist in spec-notes.md.

Earpiece built to the revised spec: numbered subagent rows with tool and last sentence, /whisper with append then send fallback (answer says by message), sent/heard/missed marks, 16 acceptance tests for A1-A15 passing with the standard five.

Build meets the spec and the checker passes, but in both live runs the whispered subagent's first tool call did not start until /earpiece-widget off, so heron, heard and 'has finished' never appeared: (1) the spec must name runs that tell the awaited tool.call refresh, the mid-tool append, the timer and the headless session apart, and stop holding next(e) on a refresh if the hook is the cause; (2) the Live script's waiting turn cannot wait in a headless session and must be rewritten so a good run is reachable; (3) say what a note appended during an in-flight tool use does; minor build items (1e+23 number echo, uncapped description) are in inspection.md.

The inspection's three faults are answered: no agent hook awaits a refresh, the Live script waits with bun timers and names control runs A and B, and the in-flight note is settled, with no contradiction, no new call and the spec at 120 lines and 15 acceptance lines; 15 notes for the machinist in spec-notes.md.

Rebuilt Earpiece to the revised spec: no hook on an agent's path awaits a refresh, overlapping refreshes are ordered by a ticket so a late one never writes over a newer one, /whisper takes 1 to 4 digits and descriptions are cut to 80 characters.

Rebuild meets the revised spec and the append works live (no hold, heron came back), but two good-run signs failed: (1) /whisper 1 too late was refused by append and the fallback send resumed the finished agent, costing a subagent turn and two unprompted main-loop turns, so the spec must stop a refused append from ending in a resume; (2) the bare /whisper still read sent after the agent had answered past the note, so the heard rule does not match what a real read returns and the Live script must show why; also word sign 2 as a time and make control run B once (the agent idled between main turns), and the A14 test timed out in one of three checker runs.

The second inspection's faults are answered: the send fallback is gone so a refused append can never resume an agent, heard is counted on assistant messages with unread shown in the bare listing, sign 2 is a time against a single control run B and A14 is split, with no contradiction, no new call and the spec at 120 lines and 15 acceptance lines; 15 notes for the machinist in spec-notes.md.

Rebuilt Earpiece to the fourth spec: the send path is gone so a refused append only answers could not be reached, heard is counted on assistant messages from a baseline read, bare /whisper runs one bounded refresh and lists unread, and A14 is split per width.

Spec is met and the live proof works (append, heron, done heard, late whisper costs nothing), but (1) bare /whisper throws in the demo engine: render.ts --do "/whisper" faults with $.clock.sleep is not a function at register.tsx:244, a call the spec does not name and docs/engine.js lacks, where the spec says draw the error card, not throw; bound the wait with $.clock.after or guard it, and test it; (2) every subagent tool cycle was about 6 s slower than in control run B (16 s against 10 s) and sign 2 fails as worded, so tool.call must await nothing before next(e) and the next live run is read by those gaps; (3) session.start and /earpiece-widget on await an unbounded refresh and should use the bounded one; details in inspection.md.

Fixed the third inspection: bare /whisper, session.start and switching on now bound their refresh with $.clock.after (no $.clock.sleep anywhere), and the agent tool.call hook awaits nothing before next(e); the extra session-only $.state key lap { begun, landed } is kept as the refresh ticket and is not in the spec's State section.

The build is unchanged since the director's ruling and still fails (a): /whisper <n> <note> answers No agent <n> on the card from the stored roster without looking (register.tsx:380-382), so in live.txt a whisper typed while the agent was on its first tool call was never appended and the agent replied NONE; (1) when the row is missing, run the bounded refresh and read again, retrying within a few seconds via $.clock.after, before answering No agent; (2) after agent.spawn look again if the refresh found no new live agent; (3) add tests for a whisper against an empty roster with a running agent and for a number that is truly absent. (c) holds: nothing throws on the demo page and the checker passes. Details in inspection.md.

Fixed the fifth inspection: /whisper <n> <note> now looks for a missing row itself (up to three bounded refreshes 750 ms apart inside a 4 s limit by $.clock.after) before answering No agent, agent.spawn looks again up to twice when its refresh found no new agent, and tests cover a whisper against an empty roster, a late-listed agent, a number that is not there and a hanging list.

Meets the director's ruling: (a) a whisper typed as the agent started was appended, (b) the bare /whisper read heard and heron came back, (c) nothing throws on the demo page; the checker passed 7 of 8 runs, its one failure being 5 s timeouts on a busy host, recorded with three other findings in inspection.md.
On the demo page, in the README and the marketplace; smoke test clean
